input.question: Why do most companies, Apple for example, not sell their own products more cheaply through their own website? Surely there is potential for more profit that way than through sellers like supermarkets?
input.ground_truth: This would be a terrible idea, because it would quickly anger all of the other vendors who sell their products. By allowing a hundred other major vendors to sell your products you're getting access to a hundred other major distribution networks that you do not have to pay for. The $30 of profit lost on every iPad sold is small change compared to the billions of dollars it would cost to try and setup a nationwide distribution system that would rival letting all of those other stores sell your product for you. Apple lost the PC wars because they were a single company making products that would not work with anyone else's stuff, fighting against the PC which would allow you to buy hardware from a thousand different companies and make them easily work together. Betamax lost to VHS in similar fashion. If you're a computer company, focus your efforts on making computers. It would be insane to spend billions trying to also be Amazon/Walmart, but only for your own products.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do most companies, Apple for example, not sell their own products more cheaply through their own website? Surely there is potential for more profit that way than through sellers like supermarkets?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a really cool toy that you made yourself. You want lots of kids to play with it and be happy.

If you put your toy in a big toy store, the store might sell it for a little bit more money than you would, but they help a lot of kids find your toy. They also help keep the toy safe and make sure it gets to the kids.

If you try to sell the toy yourself for less money on your own website, you might think you’ll make more money because you’re charging less. But here’s the thing: if you lower the price too much, you might not make enough money to pay for making the toy, or you might not have enough toys to send to everyone who wants one. Also, selling lots of toys by yourself is hard work and takes a lot of time.

Supermarkets and big stores already have lots of customers who come to them every day. So, even if they take a little bit of the money from selling your toy, they help you sell to way more people than you could by yourself.

That’s why companies like Apple let big stores and websites help them sell their products, even if the price is a bit higher, so they can reach more people and not run out of toys (or iPhones or computers) too fast.
